items.stem: What is the function of a communication system?

options.text: To store electricity until it is needed
To carry information from a sender to a receiver
To make every message reach the entire world
To turn one machine into many machines

items.explanation: A communication system has one job: to move information from a sender to a receiver. Everything in the system works toward getting the message from one place to another.

items.stem: You type a message into your phone to send to a friend. In the communication system, you are the
items.explanation: The source is where the message begins. You decide what to say and create the message, so you are the source.

items.stem: Which part of a communication system changes a message into a signal that can be sent?
items.explanation: The encoder changes the message into a signal. Your phone encodes your typed words into a pattern of signals the network can carry.

items.stem: After a message has been encoded into a signal, which part sends that signal out across a distance?
items.explanation: The transmitter sends the signal out across a distance. Your phone's antenna acts as the transmitter, sending the signal toward a cell tower.

items.stem: Your friend's phone catches the incoming signal carrying your message. Their phone is acting as the
items.explanation: The receiver picks up the signal at the far end. Your friend's phone catches the signal, so it is the receiver.

items.stem: What does the decoder do in a communication system?

options.text: It turns the signal back into a message a person can understand
It creates the original message to be sent
It chooses which channel the signal will travel through
It deletes the message after it is read

items.explanation: The decoder changes the signal back into the original message. It rebuilds your words on your friend's screen so they can read them.

items.stem: Hours after you send a text, your friend opens their phone and reads it again. Which component makes this possible?
items.explanation: Storage holds the message so it can be read or played back later. The saved text stays in the message history for your friend to reopen.

items.stem: A town needs to warn everyone about a coming storm as fast as possible. Which communication system fits best?

options.text: A printed letter mailed to each home
A private text sent to one person
A face-to-face conversation on one street

items.explanation: Radio and television are one-way, but they reach thousands of people at the same moment. For a fast, town-wide warning, wide reach matters more than being able to reply.

items.stem: Which situation calls for a two-way communication system?

options.text: Announcing the news to a large audience
Having a back-and-forth conversation with one person
Posting a notice for everyone to read

items.explanation: Two-way communication lets both people send and receive. A back-and-forth conversation needs each person to reply, so a phone call or text fits.

items.stem: Why do we still use many different communication systems instead of just one?

options.text: Each system has different benefits, so different ones fit different jobs
Every system sends the exact same kind of signal
One system can only ever send one message

items.explanation: No single system is best at everything. Each has different strengths in speed, reach, direction, storage, and cost, so the best choice depends on the situation.
